title: The Bills and Ravens Are Running Out of Time
contentHtml:
When Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson first met on the field on December 8, 2019, it felt like the rivalry that would define the next decade (or more) of the NFL. Neither young quarterback had their best game, but Jackson threw two of his three TD passes in the second half and the Ravens’ defense held off Allen and the Bills’ potential game-tying drive in the closing minutes. These were the kinds of moments that surely would decide AFC supremacy in the seasons to come.

Subscribe now

Fast-forward nearly seven years, though, and the rivalry has never quite materialized, at least not in the way we might have expected. Neither Allen nor Jackson has played in a Super Bowl, and they’ve only collectively made three AFC title games — none against each other, all losses to Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs.

As we look ahead to the 2026 NFL season, both Buffalo and Baltimore are still among the leading favorites to win the championship. But it must be asked how much longer they have for that to be the case — and whether there’s any precedent for one (much less TWO) teams to knock on the door of a Super Bowl for so long before finally getting an actual breakthrough.
